Case Study

NeoShare Local Cloud

Zero-dependency HTTP file server with threaded architecture, security hardening, and modern UX

Python 3 ThreadingHTTPServer Zero Deps Range Requests Security Hardened

Motivation

Python's built-in http.server is single-threaded — it blocks on every request. For file transfers, this means one download/upload freezes the entire server. NeoShare solves this with ThreadingHTTPServer while adding security features missing from the stdlib.

Architecture

NeoShare/
├── server.py       # ThreadedHTTPServer + custom RequestHandler
├── index.html      # Responsive UI (auto dark/light)
├── script.js       # Fetch API: upload, download, navigate, stream
├── styles.css      # Cyberpunk theme, CSS variables
└── README.md

Threading Model

from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler

class NeoShareHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    # Custom implementations for GET, POST, HEAD
    # ThreadingHTTPServer spawns one thread per connection

server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("", 8000), NeoShareHandler)
server.serve_forever()

Each connection gets its own thread — file transfers don't block other clients.

Security Hardening

Path Traversal Protection

def safe_path(self, requested_path):
    # Resolve to absolute path
    base = os.path.abspath(self.base_dir)
    target = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base, requested_path.lstrip("/")))

    # Ensure target is within base directory
    if not target.startswith(base):
        raise ForbiddenError("Directory traversal attempt")

    # Normalize (resolve symlinks, .., .)
    target = os.path.normpath(target)
    if not target.startswith(base):
        raise ForbiddenError("Directory traversal attempt")

    return target

Upload Size Limit (DoS Prevention)

MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE = 2 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024  # 2GB

def do_POST(self):
    content_length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
    if content_length > MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE:
        self.send_error(413, "Payload Too Large: 2GB limit exceeded")
        return
    # ... handle multipart upload

Custom Multipart Parser

No external dependencies — manual multipart/form-data parsing handles drag-and-drop uploads with streaming (no full body buffering).

HTTP Range Streaming (Video Seeking)

def send_file_range(self, file_path, range_header):
    file_size = os.path.getsize(file_path)
    start, end = parse_range(range_header, file_size)

    self.send_response(206)  # Partial Content
    self.send_header("Content-Range", "bytes {start}-{end}/{file_size}".format(start=start, end=end, file_size=file_size))
    self.send_header("Accept-Ranges", "bytes")
    self.send_header("Content-Length", str(end - start + 1))
    self.end_headers()

    with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
        f.seek(start)
        remaining = end - start + 1
        while remaining > 0:
            chunk = f.read(min(8192, remaining))
            if not chunk: break
            self.wfile.write(chunk)
            remaining -= len(chunk)

Enables video seeking and resume downloads in browsers — critical for media sharing.

Auto tar.gz Folder Downloads

def stream_folder_as_tar_gz(self, folder_path):
    self.send_response(200)
    self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/gzip")
    self.send_header("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=folder.tar.gz")
    self.send_header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
    self.end_headers()

    with tarfile.open(fileobj=self.wfile, mode="w|gz") as tar:
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(folder_path):
            for file in files:
                full = os.path.join(root, file)
                arcname = os.path.relpath(full, folder_path)
                tar.add(full, arcname=arcname)

Streams compressed archive on-the-fly — no temporary files, no memory spike.

Responsive UI

  • Auto theme detection: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
  • Drag-and-drop upload: HTML5 File API + Fetch
  • Virtual scrolling: Handles directories with thousands of files
  • Mobile-first: Touch-friendly, responsive breakpoints
  • Video player integration: Native with Range support

Performance

Concurrency

  • One thread per connection
  • No GIL contention on I/O (releases GIL)
  • Scales to hundreds of simultaneous clients

Memory

  • Streaming uploads (no full buffering)
  • Chunked transfer encoding
  • 2GB upload cap prevents OOM
